title: The Bookstore job and Junie Cobb's recommendation to Hughie Swift
summary: Punch recounts Tenny Wilson's wife getting him a job at the Bookstore, Junie Cobb hiring him, and a federal raid.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You never know when a Chinaman died? That's what I heard. It's disappeared, huh? Mm-hmm. Do you remember Junie Cobb?

That's the man who got me the job at Jeffrey Tabin. Two brothers, Junie Cobb and Jimmy Cobb. I was playing after, this was before I went to Golden Lily though, I just went to Chicago with the show, Mac and Mac. And we was playing at a little place called Bookstore. I tell you, her wife was playing the piano. Uh, what did this boy play so much piano? Played with us a long time. Tenny Wilson. Tenny Wilson. He had a little girl named Aurene, who was his wife. Good piano player. So she heard about me, she come and got me to play at the bookstore. Boy, all them big timers you know, knock off. See we didn't go to Waco around 11, 30, or 12 o'clock at night. It was called the bookstore. All the musicians in the woods to come in there. All performers. Junior Cobb come in and heard me play, and he went out and told Hugh Swiffer by it, well he's the guy that had the band. He was with come down and heard me. And he invited me to come to his house to a rehearsal. And I said, okay. I didn't do all that reading, but the way I was playing you know, he's crazy about it see, and singing see. So he hired me, boy that was money man. That was money, that was the most money I ever made you know. And we must have worked there about six months. The federal, what you call it, federal clothes them down, coming in, took a lot of whiskey and stuff out, dope, maybe other things. Clothes them, snipe them. Dope, huh? Yeah, them things we could all smoke, not dope like they got now. Reefers, call them reefers. They had a girl around there called a cigarette girl. They had them things under the boxes.
Law grab her and went in there and got all that stuff out of front of them. Yeah, Gene Carver got me a great job.

He played about, let me see, he played trumpet, trombone, tenor, piano, and could sing. That guy you stuff like Yeah, Gene Carver, I mean that job. He played about, let me see, he played trumpet, trombone, tenor, piano, and could sing. That guy you talking about. Yeah.
